request: Staff can record a bank-transfer expense from their phone in under 30 seconds, and the accountant sees it in Odoo without asking in WhatsApp. Context: MRH Investment (Maldives, shop + warehouse + wholesale, MVR). Different staff pay different expenses and the accountant asks in a WhatsApp group for each amount. Odoo (mrh-investment.odoo.com, saas-19.4) holds expenses as hr.expense, but 31 of 36 records have no receipt, 20 of 36 use the generic category 'Expenses', and some sit in draft, so totals are wrong. Staff have no Odoo logins and will not use Odoo screens. Jobs: Staff - record the transfer I just made, fast, on my phone, with the receipt if I have it. Accountant - see what was spent, by category and day, without asking. Owner/manager - keep bad entries out of the books (a person submits and approves drafts in Odoo).

values.observation: V1 Expenses pane with dummy data: ike-sales gains a third tab 'Expenses', reached by swipe and by the tab bar like Sales and Quotations, plum accent, ids and classes scoped to the pane; it shows the day's confirmed total, a separate pending line, the category list and the day's entries with chips 'Waiting to send', 'Not sent' (with next retry time and Retry), 'Draft', 'Approved' and 'Refused'; the Add sheet takes amount (MVR), one of the 21 categories, an optional receipt from camera or gallery, and the PIN; on a phone it matches design/expenses-tab/ in light and dark (with the D12 words); it makes no network call; an entry added on the sheet appears in the list as 'Waiting to send'; Sales and Quotations behave as before.

decisions: The Expenses pane is a third <section class="pane pane-expenses" id="pane-expenses"> added inside the existing #pager at index.html:372, after #pane-quotes (index.html:394), with a third .tab data-pane="2" in the #tabs tablist at index.html:431. One file, no build step (D9); the page stays byte-for-byte static for GitHub Pages.

Scope every new id and class to the pane with the `e-` prefix and `.pane-expenses`, following the convention the README states and index.html already keeps (`s-`/`q-`, .pane-sales/.pane-quotes). Measured: only `s` and `q` id prefixes exist today, so `e-` collides with nothing. This is what makes 'Sales and Quotations behave as before' structural rather than hopeful.

REUSE the pager IIFE at index.html:466 unchanged for swipe and tap: it is already generic over tabs.length (`var last = tabs.length - 1`), .pane at index.html:52 already carries flex 0 0 100% and scroll-snap-align/stop, and the roving-tabindex keydown handler at index.html:509 is bounded by `last`. No new swipe code.

EXTEND only the two places in that IIFE and its CSS that are hardcoded to two panes: sync() at index.html:491 blends `color-mix(in srgb, var(--quotes) P%, var(--sales))`, which is wrong for a third pane, and the accent rules at index.html:68-69 cover only [data-pane="0"] and [data-pane="1"]. Widen the blend to interpolate between the two accents adjacent to the current scroll position and add a [data-pane="2"] plum rule.

Add --expenses accent tokens alongside --sales/--quotes at index.html:30 (light) and index.html:41 (dark): #8a3f64 light and #d98ab0 dark. Both were measured as the dominant accent in design/expenses-tab/Main.dc.html and MainDark.dc.html (9 occurrences each), not chosen by eye. .pane-expenses sets --accent: var(--expenses), exactly as .pane-sales and .pane-quotes do at index.html:54 and :56.

REUSE window.ikeDay (index.html:450) so the Expenses pane follows the same day as Sales: it subscribes with ikeDay.on('expenses', fn) and broadcasts with ikeDay.set(date, 'expenses'). No new day-indexing and no second source of truth for the selected day.

V1 ships dummy data held in a pane-local closure and nothing else: no fetch, no XHR, no beacon, no localStorage read of a service response. Measured context for the falsifier: the page as a whole already issues four network requests on load (two Google Fonts, ike-data sales.json, ike-data quotations.json), so 'makes no network call' is scoped to the pane and is checked as 'no request beyond that pre-existing set'.

The dummy day carries at least one entry per chip so that one page load exhibits all five of D12's states: 'Waiting to send', 'Not sent' (with its next retry time and a Retry button), 'Draft', 'Approved', 'Refused'. The Retry button is inert in V1; its behaviour is V3/V4's.

Apply D12's wording over the approved screens: the design's 'Posted' (4 occurrences in Status.dc.html) becomes 'Draft'/'Approved'/'Refused', the legend becomes 'Waiting > Draft > Approved', and the Add sheet drops 'Posts straight to Odoo as a bank transfer.' (AddSheet.dc.html). Their absence is part of the expected observation, so the design screens cannot silently leak back in.

The hero carries the day's confirmed total and, beneath it, a separate pending line — a deliberate departure from design/expenses-tab/Main.dc.html, which shows only one figure. D11 counts approved/posted/in_payment/paid as confirmed and draft/submitted as pending, so a single figure could not agree with the chips.

The Add sheet takes amount (MVR, numeric), a category select carrying exactly D7's 21 names, an optional receipt, and the PIN. The receipt offers two controls, 'Take photo' (<input type="file" accept="image/*" capture="environment">) and 'Gallery' (<input type="file" accept="image/*">); the capture attribute is the whole of the camera claim and is readable from the DOM, since no headless run has a camera.

Posting from the sheet appends the entry to the pane's local list chipped 'Waiting to send' and closes the sheet. The PIN is neither validated nor stored in V1 — it is only collected; validation is V2's, over the Worker.

Introduce package.json with playwright as the only devDependency and .gitignore node_modules, so the oracle can drive a real browser while the deployed artefact stays static. Probed: `npx -y -p playwright@1.63.0 node <script>` fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND because npx does not place the package on the child's resolution path, so a repo-local manifest is the only route that actually runs.
Follow the file's existing paradigm: ES5 IIFEs over closures, var, no classes and no own prototypes, matching window.ikeDay (index.html:450) and the pager (index.html:466).

values.observation: V2 Save-first service: a Cloudflare Worker with D1 answers 'saved' for an entry (amount, category, optional receipt, PIN, client entry id) only after the entry and its receipt are stored durably; it refuses a wrong PIN, a request from any origin other than the ike-sales page, an unknown category, and an amount that is not a positive MVR number, and it rate-limits wrong PINs; the same client entry id sent twice stores one entry, not two; it serves the 21 categories and the day's entries with their status; the PIN is a Worker secret, and a changed secret takes effect at once without touching saved entries.

V3 Pane on real data: the Expenses pane takes its 21 categories and the day's entries with status from the service, and the day's confirmed total, pending total and category list from ike-data/data/expenses.json; 'Post expense' on a phone saves through the service, closes the sheet and shows the entry as 'Waiting to send', inside the 30-second budget; a wrong PIN or an unreachable service keeps the typed entry in the sheet with a plain message, and the page never shows an entry as saved that the service did not confirm.

values.observation: V4 Odoo sync: for each saved entry the Worker creates exactly one DRAFT hr.expense (employee Ahmed Rashad id 1, the chosen category, the amount in MVR, company-paid by bank transfer, dated per D16, the receipt attached when given, and a unique mark naming the entry) and never submits, approves, posts or pays it; a failed or unanswered Odoo call leaves the entry saved as 'Not sent' with its next retry time, it retries on schedule and on Retry, and a retry after a create whose answer was lost finds the existing expense by its mark instead of creating a second; once created the entry shows 'Draft' and appears as pending in expenses.json; the Odoo API key exists only as a Worker secret.

values.observation: V5 Status read-back: every 15 minutes, on the same Worker schedule as the sync retries, the Worker reads the Odoo state of its entries that still show 'Draft' with one read-only call and sets each chip by D12: draft or submitted stays 'Draft', approved/posted/in_payment/paid becomes 'Approved', refused becomes 'Refused'; an entry in Approved or Refused is not read again; an Odoo failure during read-back changes no chip and is tried again on the next run; the Worker writes nothing to Odoo in this step.
